headline: Preference and reinforcement learning steer generative models for biomolecular design
label: Generative Protein Sequence Design
summary: Recent preprints and a publication embed physical validity and multi-objective scoring directly inside generative optimization loops.
synthesis: The dominant thread is reinforcement or preference optimization of generative models against explicit, non-differentiable objectives. The docking study fine-tunes a diffusion-based docking model (DiffDock-Pocket) on physical validity and interaction terms. The inverse folding study proposes Symmetric Self-play Preference Optimization, which decouples multiple structural objectives across separate preference models. The AI-MedCraft framework applies Pareto-guided reinforcement learning with physics-aware scoring to multi-objective small-molecule design. What is new across these items is the treatment of objectives as separable, explicitly scored signals inside the generative loop, rather than as a single differentiable loss. The summaries do not report experimental validation of the resulting designs, so performance claims remain unsupported here.
